clue.text: Returning part quietly, is ahead of time — he says little

indicators.note: says the letters before it come in front of the abbreviation for time
returning sends the word part back the way it came, read right to left

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A cryptic portrait of a reticent man, assembled from bits about parts, quiet and time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' reverses PART to TRAP. In crosswords 'part' rarely means a role here; it is simply the word read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappist monks keep a strict rule of silence, so a member of that order is someone who speaks very little.

clue.text: Hill creature finally moved fast

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word creature

explanation.surface: An animal on a hillside finally bolts away at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hilltop, common in place names in the south-west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tore is the past tense of tear in the sense of rushing along at great speed.

clue.text: Some bar types affecting interest in painting?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pub regulars who pretend to care about painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pretentious who makes a show of caring for the arts is described as artsy or affected in taste.

clue.text: Support Religious Instruction, uplifting routine for owner

parts.note: a prop is something that holds a thing up
RI is the school-subject abbreviation for religious instruction

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means the word for routine is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rote is mechanical routine, as in learning by rote

explanation.surface: A school owner backing RE lessons with a cheerful routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' looks like praise for the routine, but in a down entry it turns ROTE into ETOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the person who holds legal title to a business or property.

clue.text: Source of music in street before beginning of October

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: beginning of picks the opening letter of the word October

explanation.surface: Music heard on the street before the start of October.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a hi-fi system, the equipment a household plays music through.

clue.text: Clothing, women's, needing attention

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women, as on clothing labels
to give an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Women's clothes in need of some care.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops group garments under labels like menswear or sportswear, using the word as a noun for clothes.

clue.text: European, on rise, meets eastern Democrat, much-admired

indicators.note: in a down clue, on rise means the word meets is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A rising European politician meets an eastern Democrat and is widely admired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On rise' looks like a politician's career climbing, but in a down entry it signals the word read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To be held in esteem is to be highly regarded, so the adjective means greatly respected.

clue.text: Series of notes seeking an answer?

definitions.text: Series of notes seeking an answer?

parts.words: Series of notes seeking an answer?
parts.note: the musical notes a phone plays are calling for someone to pick up, or answer, the call

explanation.surface: A musical phrase that seems to pose a question.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a melody ending on a questioning phrase; the answer to be sought is that of someone picking up the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile phone plays a short tune when called, prompting its owner to pick up.

clue.text: Restricted to fixed amount, an editor's upset

indicators.note: upset means the letters of an editor are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor is annoyed at having his word count capped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' sounds like the editor's mood, but it signals the anagram; the 's is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wartime food was allocated by ration, each person allowed only a set quantity.

clue.text: Turning heads in surprise

indicators.note: turning means the slang word for heads is read in the other direction

parts.note: nuts is slang for heads, as in a nut on the shoulders

explanation.surface: Heads turn in astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or astonish them so they are momentarily dazed.

clue.text: The German complaint following off-line event maybe?

indicators.note: following says the word for complaint comes after the German article

parts.note: der is a German word for the
an ailment is a medical complaint

explanation.surface: A German illness that strikes after going offline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off-line' suggests being disconnected from the internet; here it is a train leaving the rails, with a question mark showing this is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: When a train comes off its rails, that accident is literally an off-line event.

clue.text: Disrespectful library oddly ignored event including monarch

indicators.note: oddly ignored drops the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of library, keeping the even ones
including means the word event holds the monarch's letters within it

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A library event attended by royalty turns out to be cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly ignored' keeps the even letters only. The monarch is the late Queen, Elizabeth Regina, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing a lack of proper respect, especially toward serious or sacred things, is a synonym for rude.

clue.text: Atop her a strange item of headgear

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of atop her a are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A peculiar thing perched on top of her head.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapsible top hat worn to the theatre in the nineteenth century, an example of a hat.

clue.text: Friend coming across artist, Lely, almost exact likeness

indicators.note: coming across means the word for friend spans the abbreviation for an artist, holding it inside

parts.note: pal is an informal word for friend
RA is a Royal Academician, a British artist

indicators.note: almost means the painter's name loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A friend meeting the portrait painter Lely, who nearly captured him exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Peter Lely was a 17th-century court painter; RA (Royal Academician) is the stock abbreviation for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A parallel is a close counterpart or something very similar, a match in another context.

clue.text: Mercury, say, element at outset brought into factory

indicators.note: brought into means the letter goes inside the word for a factory

parts.note: a plant is an industrial works or factory

indicators.note: at outset takes the opening letter of the word element

explanation.surface: The chemical element mercury, from the outset, brought into a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mercury' and 'element' tempt a chemistry reading; Mercury is instead the nearest planet to the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is the smallest world in our solar system, one example of the class.

clue.text: Surrender cases of china, valuable, ill-gotten

indicators.note: cases are the outsides, so take the first and last letters of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Handing back boxes of valuable stolen porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: To cave in is a phrasal verb for yielding or giving way under pressure.

clue.text: Outrageous claim over English evil intent

indicators.note: in a down clue, over says the rearranged word sits above the abbreviation
outrageous suggests the word claim is wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: An outrageous English claim made with spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to do harm to others, a deliberate ill will.

clue.text: Referring to a relative, competent, fair

parts.note: re means concerning or referring to, as in a letter heading
a son is a family relative
able means capable or competent

explanation.surface: A reference for a relative who is competent and fair-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensible, moderate price or judgement is called fair, meaning just and acceptable.

clue.text: Eyelid problem, sore, that you experienced initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Asking about the painful eyelid you had.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the edge of the eyelid, caused by an infected gland.

clue.text: Try to create favourable impression — bring up drinks

indicators.note: in a down clue, bring up means the word for drinks is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nips are small drinks of spirits

explanation.surface: Offering drinks to win people over.
explanation.definitionFit: Press officers put a slant on news to make it look good, the practice of presenting things positively.

clue.text: Hours with the Spanish male tiller

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish man at the tiller for hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiller is the lever that steers a boat, the steering gear also called by this name.

clue.text: Avoid team backing favourites

parts.note: a side is a sports team

indicators.note: backing means the word for favourites is read in reverse

parts.note: a teacher's pets are their favourites

explanation.surface: Steering clear of a team supporting the favourites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like supporting the favourites, but it reverses PETS to STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep an issue or a tackle is to evade it by moving aside.

clue.text: In Bristol, lonely, ring repeatedly

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the words that follow it

explanation.surface: A lonely figure in Bristol rings a bell again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristol is a city in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell tolls when it is struck slowly and steadily over and over, as for a funeral.

clue.text: Lying scattered in "Bravo", unusual Western

parts.note: Bravo is B in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of western are arranged in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A western film titled Bravo, which is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestrewn means covered with things strewn about, as a floor with litter.
